findings.statement: CXCR2 tops the convergence ranking: up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]) and higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa of the same patient (paired log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]); the change holds after adjustment for segment, age and sex. Caveat: CXCR2 is a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk rise most likely reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than a change inside the epithelium, although it is tractable (several dual CXCR1 and CXCR2 antagonists reached phase 2 or phase 3).

CXCR1, the partner receptor of CXCR2, is up in most cohorts and shows a strong local inflamed-vs-non-inflamed paired change (log2FC [gene=CXCR1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.193]). It is a neutrophil-derived signal and shares the drug class with CXCR2.

CXCL8, the main ligand of CXCR1 and CXCR2, is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864]) and the change holds after adjustment in the MSCCR cohort (adjusted log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.499]). It has no genetic support, and the signal is mixed epithelial and myeloid, so it is an inflammation marker more than a causal target.

IDO1 is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118]), holds after adjustment, and is also seen as protein in an independent proteomics study (log2 ratio [gene=IDO1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.917]). The tryptophan/IFN-gamma axis is therefore reproduced at RNA and protein level; the protein change is much smaller than the RNA change.

CHI3L1 is one of the largest and most consistent increases (up in all eight cohorts, significant in each) with a strong local component (paired inflamed vs non-inflamed log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.6182]). At protein level the rise is far smaller (log2 ratio [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607]) and the authors did not call it significant, so protein support is weaker than the RNA.

HMGCS2 (epithelial ketogenesis) is lost in all eight cohorts and the loss is local to inflamed mucosa: it is absent in non-inflamed mucosa versus control (padj [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.675]) but strong in the paired inflamed-vs-non-inflamed comparison (log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.9508]). Proteomics confirms it (log2 ratio [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]), and it holds after adjustment. This is a metabolic inflammation-activity biomarker, not a target.

DUOX2 is among the strongest epithelial increases (pooled log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.412], up in all eight cohorts), holds after adjustment, and is seen as protein (log2 ratio [gene=DUOX2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=1.468]). It is mainly an epithelial host-defence/redox signal, so it is less affected by immune-cell infiltration than the neutrophil genes.

JAK2 has strong genetic support and a drug history but only a modest and reproducible RNA rise (pooled log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.874], up in all eight cohorts; paired local change [gene=JAK2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.4031]). Its rank rests on genetics and tractability, not on a large expression change, and the signalling effect is post-transcriptional.

S100A8 (calprotectin subunit) is up in all eight cohorts and replicates at protein level (log2 ratio [gene=S100A8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=2.749]). It is neutrophil/myeloid-derived, consistent with the established stool calprotectin marker, so it reports infiltrating-cell burden rather than an intrinsic tissue change.

MMP3 shows one of the largest pooled increases (log2FC [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.901], up in all eight cohorts) with a strong local paired change; stromal/fibroblast tissue-remodelling signal, with broad MMP inhibitors having poor clinical tolerability history.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in all eight cohorts and is supported by genetics and literature, so it is an IFN-gamma-response feature of inflamed mucosa. Immune-cell and epithelial contributions are mixed in bulk data; checkpoint agonism, not inhibition, would be the therapeutic direction.

caveats: Bulk RNA cannot separate infiltrating neutrophils and immune cells from tissue-intrinsic change; CXCR1/2, CXCL8, S100A8/9, TREM1 and IL1B are likely neutrophil/myeloid-driven.
Heterogeneity between cohorts is high (I2 above 0.9 for most top genes); microarray fold changes are compressed so only direction and significance are comparable across cohorts.
Protein replication comes from one small proteomics study and many genes are not measured there; CHI3L1 did not reach the authors' significance call.
Adjusted and paired analyses come only from the MSCCR cohort; paediatric cohorts are at diagnosis and may be more severe.
